steps.en: What you see: The ECG trace runs with the echo from the same heartbeat. The QRS starts ventricular systole: the mitral and tricuspid valves shut, the ventricles squeeze, and the aortic and pulmonary valves open. The T wave ends systole: the outflow valves shut, the ventricles relax, and the inflow valves open for filling.
Sounds and trace landmarks: Each sound and wave lines up with a valve event.
Trace standards and timing: ECG paper speed 25 mm per s with calibration 10 mm per mV.
Mark end diastole at the start of the QRS and end systole at aortic valve closure.
Measure chamber diameters at end diastole and wall thickness at end diastole.

Pitfalls: A noisy ECG trace mistriggers timing, so recheck lead contact before measuring dyssynchrony or strain. In atrial fibrillation every beat differs, so average measurements over at least five beats.

todo.en: Event order in one beat: P wave: the atria squeeze and top up the ventricles.
QRS start: the inflow valves shut and end diastole is marked for measurements.
ST segment: the outflow valves are open and blood is ejected.
T wave end: the outflow valves shut and end systole is marked.
After the T wave: the inflow valves open and the ventricles fill.
